gen-nixie-one-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans stands tall, its lowercase sturdy and its e opening clearly to the right. Nixie One draws delicate tube-like outlines that hold their thickness through every bend, while Merriweather Sans carries the weight.
gen-nixie-one-fs-public-sans: Thin, tube-like strokes that never change width give Nixie One its retro-tech glow. Public Sans follows with a hefty lowercase and broad counters, so a long stretch of text feels sturdy and unhurried.
gen-nixie-one-fs-supreme: Nixie One looks like outlines drawn in a single width, nostalgic and gap-filled, over Supreme's thick, heavy-looking text. Crisp against delicate.
gen-nixie-one-general-sans: Nixie One brings a retro-tech feel with open curves and a constant stroke, while General Sans fills its lines with a tall x-height. Reading on goes smoothly.
gen-nixie-one-gf-orbit: Retro glow meets floating letters. Nixie One is best at nostalgic open curves of constant stroke, whereas Orbit does its best work with rope-like consistency and curves that stop short of closing.
gen-nixie-one-gf-science-gothic: Retro-tech lines, then crisp spacing. Science Gothic keeps stroke ends far apart and avoids thick and thin parts, so a longer passage feels like reading one letter at a time.
gen-nixie-one-gf-syncopate: Nixie One has a nostalgic, retro-tech look, with open curves and one constant stroke from top to baseline. Syncopate answers with technical-pen steadiness and rung-like spacing.
gen-nixie-one-manrope: Nostalgic in feel, Nixie One draws open curves with a constant stroke from top to baseline. Manrope adds bright gaps at every curve and a minimal step up from lowercase to capitals.
gen-nixie-one-work-sans: Constant-stroke tubes with open gaps define Nixie One. Work Sans feels contemporary beside it, with c tips that never creep toward touching and a mean line set high, so the two sit modern against nostalgic.
gen-orbitron-archivo: Neon-tube precision, spread wide. Orbitron earns its keep big and short, letters far apart with a large eye on every e, while Archivo's outward-opening curves and commanding x-height handle the reading.
